milestone: M5 — both-host operations, capacity qualification, public release engineering

race.note: A separate run that overlapped a binary rebuild reported one rtc failure ("peer failed to connect"). It was not a race: the package passes on three consecutive race-enabled runs and in the clean full run. The cause was the rebuild replacing the test binary underneath a running suite, not a product defect.

capacity.population: 4 accounts, 3 channels, 24 messages, 2 reactions, 3 direct conversations
capacity.reason: One development host over loopback. The master plan budgets are stated for four cores, 8 GiB, a LAN and 100 Mbit/s symmetric. No ramp, no peak, no soak, no media, no host qualification.

release_engineering.sbom: THIRD-PARTY-SBOM.json (CycloneDX 1.5), generated from the same component set as the notices, version-stamped per release
release_engineering.connection_path_reported: A call reports direct, STUN or relayed, so whether it is relayed is answerable from the client.

not_established: No host qualification: no Windows host, no Linux Docker host, no Tailscale peer. docs/host-qualification.md is written and has not been run.
No qualifying capacity figure: the reference profile is 250 accounts, 100 channels, a million messages, 100 clients, a two-hour peak and a 24-hour soak. None was run.
No monitoring or alert delivery: a configured alert is not a delivered alert, and none was verified.
No container runtime qualification: static Dockerfile checks are not Docker runtime.
No signed Windows download, no canonical public repository or registry identity, and no Git remote configured in this environment.
No independent security or accessibility review, no physical-device observation, and no beta.
